questions.question: Which statement is the strongest production invariant for a prompt version?
options: It is ready when one example sounds fluent
It is ready when it is longer than the previous prompt
It is ready only when representative evaluation and every required gate pass
It is ready when the model explains its reasoning
questions.explanation: Prompt behavior must be demonstrated across relevant traffic and risk slices. Fluency, length, and generated explanations are not release evidence.

questions.question: What makes a conversational turn different from an isolated model request?
options: It carries bounded session state, partial delivery, and continuity expectations across turns
It always uses a larger model
It never needs authentication
It stores every token forever
questions.explanation: A conversation adds state and lifecycle contracts; those contracts must remain explicit and bounded.

questions.question: What is the core authority boundary in function calling?
options: The model proposes an action, while deterministic application code validates and authorizes execution.
Valid JSON gives the model permission to execute the named API.
The tool description replaces runtime authorization.
The model should receive the service credential so it can retry directly.
questions.explanation: A tool call is untrusted structured output. Application code owns identity, policy, credentials, execution, and side effects.

questions.question: What is the core product invariant for inline completion?
options: Typing never waits for inference, and generated text enters the document only after explicit acceptance.
Every eligible keystroke must display a suggestion.
The server owns the draft while a request is active.
Late suggestions should be inserted once the user pauses.
questions.explanation: Completion is an optional proposal path. The editor and writer remain authoritative even when every suggestion dependency fails.

questions.question: What is the core production invariant for machine translation?
options: Release only when meaning and protected facts remain attributable to the source.
Always choose the candidate with the highest model probability.
Use one global quality score for every language.
Translate every request even when the language pair is unsupported.
questions.explanation: Fluency and model preference do not excuse changed numbers, missing placeholders, unsafe additions, or unsupported source meaning.
